gaps.sentence: 'I must finish this today,' she said. She said she ___ finish it that day.
gaps.explanation: Must expressing obligation usually becomes had to in reported speech; 'today' becomes 'that day'.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
gaps.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

gaps.sentence: "It was your fault." — They blamed me ___ the accident.
